title: Reviewing Your Birthday Message
credits: Faith Pirlo wrote this lesson for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Recently, our readers and listeners wrote many lovely messages about their birthdays.
sentences.zh: 最近，我们的读者和听众写了许多关于他们生日的温馨留言。

sentences.en: We have been reading all of them.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在阅读所有这些留言。

sentences.en: Most messages are happy.
sentences.zh: 大多数留言都充满欢乐。

sentences.en: You wrote about gifts you received, the people who celebrated with you, or where and how you celebrated.
sentences.zh: 你们写到了收到的礼物、与你们一同庆祝的人，或是庆祝的地点和方式。

sentences.en: Some messages seemed sad.
sentences.zh: 有些留言则显得忧伤。

sentences.en: Some of you do not get to celebrate your birthdays.
sentences.zh: 有些人无法庆祝自己的生日。

sentences.en: Other messages were a mix of sad and happy.
sentences.zh: 有些留言则是悲喜交加。

sentences.en: In this week's Everyday Grammar, we are looking at Farhana’s message about her birthday. She wrote:
sentences.zh: 在本周的"每日语法"中，我们来看看法尔哈纳关于她生日的留言。她写道：

sentences.en: My birthday was on last 23 march.
sentences.zh: 我的生日是上个月23号三月。

sentences.en: This was my 27th birthday.
sentences.zh: 这是我的第27个生日。

sentences.en: In my birthday no one wished me except my younger sister.
sentences.zh: 在我生日那天，除了我妹妹，没有人向我祝贺。

sentences.en: And actually there was no devise for this day.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上那天并没有什么特别的安排。

sentences.en: I spent my whole day as like it is a normal day.
sentences.zh: 我整天都像平常日子一样度过。

sentences.en: Sometimes i felt sad and sometimes i wasn't.
sentences.zh: 有时候我会感到难过，有时候则不会。

sentences.en: Let us start at the beginning. Farhana writes:
sentences.zh: 让我们从头说起。法尔哈纳写道：

sentences.en: My birthday was on last 23 march.
sentences.zh: 我的生日是上个月23号三月。

sentences.en: We suggest changing this sentence to the present tense to say when your birthday is.
sentences.zh: 我们建议把这句话改成现在时，来说明你的生日是哪一天。

sentences.en: My birthday is March 23.
sentences.zh: 我的生日是3月23日。

sentences.en: In American English, the usual order for dates is month, day, year.
sentences.zh: 在美式英语中，日期的通常顺序是月、日、年。

sentences.en: So instead of “23 March,” Americans usually say “March 23.”
sentences.zh: 所以美国人通常不说"23 March"，而是说"March 23"。

sentences.en: You used the past tense in this sentence:
sentences.zh: 你在这个句子中使用了过去时态：

sentences.en: This was my 27th birthday.
sentences.zh: 这一天是我的27岁生日。

sentences.en: Another way we can say how old we are, is to use the past tense of the verb “turn.”
sentences.zh: 我们还可以用动词"turn"的过去式来表达我们的年龄。

sentences.en: I turned 27 this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年满27岁了。

sentences.en: Here, “turn” means to reach or pass into a new age.
sentences.zh: 在这里，"turn"的意思是达到或进入一个新的年龄。

sentences.en: Next Farhana wrote this:
sentences.zh: 接下来法尔哈纳写了这样一句话：

sentences.en: We can change the word order of this sentence to make it clearer.
sentences.zh: 我们可以改变这个句子的语序，让它更清楚。

sentences.en: No one wished me happy birthday, except my younger sister.
sentences.zh: 除了我妹妹，没有人祝我生日快乐。

sentences.en: Instead of a prepositional phrase, “In my birthday,” we can just start the sentence with “No one.”
sentences.zh: 与其用介词短语"In my birthday"，我们不如直接用"No one"来开头。

sentences.en: “No one” is an indefinite pronoun meaning "no person."
sentences.zh: "No one"是一个不定代词，意思是"没有人"。

sentences.en: You could also use the pronoun “nobody.”
sentences.zh: 你也可以使用代词"nobody"。

sentences.en: Onto the next sentence:
sentences.zh: 来看下一句：

sentences.en: And actually there was no devise for this day.
sentences.zh: 而且这天其实并没有事先的安排。

sentences.en: “To devise” is a verb meaning to plan or think up something.
sentences.zh: "devise"是一个动词，意思是计划或想出某事。

sentences.en: You were close!
sentences.zh: 你差不多对了！

sentences.en: But in this sentence we need a noun.
sentences.zh: 但在这个句子中我们需要一个名词。

sentences.en: And we find it in the definition of devise: plan.
sentences.zh: 而我们在devise的定义中找到了它：计划。

sentences.en: Actually, there was no plan for the day.
sentences.zh: 其实，这天并没有事先的计划。

sentences.en: If you wanted to use the word devise, however, you could!
sentences.zh: 不过，如果你想用devise这个词，你也是可以的！

sentences.en: It would come right after “plan” in the sentence.
sentences.zh: 它会紧跟在句子中的"plan"之后。

sentences.en: Actually, there was no plan devised for the day.
sentences.zh: 其实，这一天并没有事先安排好计划。

sentences.en: Farhana’s next sentence is:
sentences.zh: Farhana的下一句话是：

sentences.en: I spent my whole day as like it is a normal day.
sentences.zh: 我整天都过得像平常的一天一样。

sentences.en: We should make a few changes to this sentence.
sentences.zh: 我们应该对这句话做几处修改。

sentences.en: “As” and “like” are both used to make comparisons between nouns.
sentences.zh: “as”和“like”都用来在名词之间进行比较。

sentences.en: “As” is an adverb, and “like” is a preposition.
sentences.zh: “as”是副词，而“like”是介词。

sentences.en: We only need one of these to make the comparison.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要其中一种就可以进行比较。

sentences.en: We can say:
sentences.zh: 我们可以这样说：

sentences.en: I spent my whole day like it was a normal day.
sentences.zh: 我整天都过得像平常的一天。

sentences.en: Let us look now at Farhana’s last sentence:
sentences.zh: 现在让我们来看Farhana的最后一句话：

sentences.en: Sometimes i felt sad and sometimes i wasn't.
sentences.zh: 有时候我会感到难过，有时候则不会。

sentences.en: We suggest changing this sentence to:
sentences.zh: 我们建议把这句话改成：

sentences.en: Now the two parts of the sentence agree in verb use.
sentences.zh: 现在句子的两部分在动词使用上保持一致了。

sentences.en: Also, We always capitalize the pronoun “I” in sentences.
sentences.zh: 另外，我们总是把句子中的代词“我”大写。

sentences.en: We used the conjunction “but” with “other times” only to create more contrast.
sentences.zh: 我们使用连词“but”搭配“other times”只是为了制造更多的对比。

sentences.en: It is also correct to write:
sentences.zh: 这样写也是正确的：

sentences.en: Sometimes I felt sad and sometimes I didn’t.
sentences.zh: 有时候我会难过，有时候则不会。

sentences.en: Now, let's hear the revised message about Farhana's birthday:
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们来听一下关于Farhana生日的修改后的消息：

sentences.en: My birthday is March 23.
sentences.zh: 我的生日是3月23日。

sentences.en: I turned 27 this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年27岁了。

sentences.en: No one wished me happy birthday except my younger sister.
sentences.zh: 没有人祝我生日快乐，除了我妹妹。

sentences.en: Actually, there was no plan for the day.
sentences.zh: 其实，这一天并没有什么安排。

sentences.en: I spent my whole day like it was a normal day.
sentences.zh: 我整天都像普通一天那样度过。

sentences.en: Sometimes I felt sad, but other times, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 有时我会感到难过，但有时也不会。

sentences.en: Thank you Farhana for your message.
sentences.zh: 法尔哈娜，谢谢你的祝福。

sentences.en: We would like to wish you a happy birthday, early, for next year.
sentences.zh: 我们想提前为你庆祝明年的生日。

sentences.en: I’m Caty Weaver.
sentences.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

glossary.def: to think of; to come up with, to invent or plan
to begin (a word or name) with a capital letter
a difference between things or people that are being compared
a person who appears in a movie, book, film...
